Tsering stops the train to listen near the rock opening.

A fracture races across the snow slope.
Tsering cuts the lead rope and directs the team across-slope.
Mules scatter as the avalanche bears down.
Tsering and Indy brace together on the wooden pack saddle.

Indy and Tsering count the surviving pack mules.
The gray mule stands apart as the Junkers passes high above.
At dawn, the gray treeless valley opens below them, smoke rising from camp.
Tsering names Lhari but avoids looking at the sacred ridge.
At midday the wind stops and the distant camp flags fall limp.
From behind granite, they observe tents, a generator shed, mule line and enclosure.
Tsering corrects Indy’s camp sketch and the direction of the wind.
A broad-shouldered figure rises from the timber-shored fenced pen.

Pemba approaches at dusk with both hands raised and empty.

Pemba sketches the route into the German camp in the dirt.
The searchlight passes overhead while the three stay hidden.

Pemba asks Indy to record his brother’s name correctly.
Pemba shows the trail fork where he will hide the crate.

Inside the crate, Indy watches through a small knot-hole.
Pemba taps twice on the lid to signal Indy to stay still.
Pemba walks beside the mule train, humming to the animals.
A German sergeant counts crates at the checkpoint.
The closed crate is set inside a storage tent at dusk.

The figure pours out the cup and saves the rice inside it.

Indy passes the lit, noisy mess tent while listening to the soldiers.

Indy slips into Kessler’s survey tent.
Kessler’s precise tent: maps, two cups, survey table and locked trunk.
Indy picks the trunk lock and discovers a leather folder.
Indy studies the anthropometric photographs and calipers.
He carefully returns a small personal photograph to its place.
Indy reads Kessler’s private 1939 field report.
A soldier searches the tent; Indy hides beneath the cot.
Kessler enters and finds Indy beside the open trunk.
Two guards raise rifles as Indy stops reaching for his revolver.
Kessler tidies the room and restores every item to order.
Kessler tells Indy he expected a thief, not a scholar.
Kessler explains why he fears Berlin will misuse the discovery.
Indy nudges a brass weight; Kessler corrects it without looking.
Indy and Kessler argue over a scholarly footnote.
Kessler asks Indy to examine the being and give an honest judgment.
Kessler offers a sweet sent by his sister in Zurich.
Kessler invites Indy to walk to the pen; Indy asks whether it has a name.
Kessler leads Indy and two riflemen to the enclosure.
Kessler shows Indy the tall figure seated against the far timber.
The captive looks at Indy with patient, humanlike attention.
Indy notices scratches at seated height on the post.
Indy counts repeated groups of tally marks.
He spots bright worn bolt heads at the lower pen corner.
The captive rests its chin on its knees while Indy studies it.

The soldier quietly says he wants to go home.

Indy hides behind a shoulder-high rock as a dog patrol approaches.
The yellow dog sniffs toward Indy’s hiding place.
Indy tosses bread aside to redirect the dog.
Tsering mends her coat as Indy tells her what happened.
Tsering stops sewing when Indy describes the photograph.
Tsering asks about her brother’s chipped front tooth.
Tsering draws the long-hidden letter from an inner pocket.
Indy unfolds Norbu’s letter by the ridge fire.
Norbu’s letter recalls bones found in the ice above camp.

Indy and Tsering sit sleepless beside Norbu’s letter and a small fire.
Tsering grips her knife, angry and intent on confronting Kessler.
Indy argues for justice and getting the truth into the open.
Tsering quietly pulls the blanket back over Indy’s shoulder.

Tsering recalls Norbu’s stubbornness and singing.
Pemba arrives breathless with urgent news.
Tsering guides Indy through a silent Lee-Enfield bolt cycle.
Pemba describes the polite German flyers and their questions.
The group checks their tools, rifle and fourteen rounds.

They observe the transport plane and gravel landing strip.
Six ground crew sit beside the petrol drums near the plane.
Two rocket troopers appear above the eastern ridge.
Indy and Tsering run for the narrow shale gully.
Indy counts the troopers’ remaining flight time on his watch.
Tsering raises her rifle; Indy signals her to wait.
Flame licks the gully overhang as Indy keeps counting.

Indy and Tsering discuss exploiting the difference between Voss and Kessler.
Tsering sets the seventh-bell schedule for entering the camp.
Indy walks alone toward the camp at dusk.
Sentries search Indy and return the red wrist cord.

Voss kneels at a guy rope as Indy quietly pockets a pencil.
At the pen, the captive watches Voss and Indy with patient disinterest.
Voss speaks of his daughters and wanting to explain the discovery to them.
Indy points out the tally marks; Voss finally notices their meaning.
Voss ends the walk and orders guards to escort Indy out.
Stoll guides Indy toward the broken-ground edge and threatens a fall.

Indy uses his belt buckle to trap Stoll’s forearm.
Tsering charges in on the mule as the dinner bell rings.
Tsering and Indy escape through the north perimeter on the mule.
Indy, Tsering and Pemba plan the night raid over a dirt map.
Tsering oils her Lee-Enfield; Pemba brings stolen dried apricots.
The team moves toward the generator shed after midnight.
Pemba is captured while Indy restrains Tsering from rushing toward the guards.
Tsering shoots a trooper’s cylinder, sparing the young man.
Indy and Tsering approach the guarded trunk at the mule line.
Indy opens the trunk and recovers Kessler’s folder and his revolver.
Flaming harness troopers rise as searchlights sweep the camp.
The creature calmly loosens its iron pen strap under the floodlights.
Tsering cuts the mule picket rope; the herd surges through camp.
Indy cuts the generator’s fuel line, plunging the camp into darkness.
The lights fail as the creature tears free of the pen.
Leutnant Falk descends on his flame pack and confronts Indy.
Indy takes cover behind steel drums while Falk hovers above.
Indy grabs Falk’s boots as the harness lifts them into the sky.
Indy climbs toward the harness controls as the fuel gauge falls.
A cross-valve turn sends the flying pair corkscrewing over camp.
Falk and Indy crash into the mess tent and the cook intervenes.
The creature offers Indy its cup of rice; he raises an open hand.
Tsering catches Indy as the crevasse ledge gives way beneath him.
Indy descends into the crevasse to recover the satchel.
Tsering hauls Indy and the satchel over the icy rim as Kessler watches.
Tsering confronts Kessler at the crevasse; Indy learns he did not fire.
Kessler writes and signs his confession in the snow.
Jo arrives in a flashbulb afterglow with her Speed Graphic camera.
Jo introduces herself to Tsering and offers to witness the confession.
Jo photographs each page of Kessler’s confession by torchlight.
Voss’s soldiers gather on the snowfield to capture the creature alive.
The creature lifts the capture net and scatters its rope-holders.
Jo’s camera flash blinds the diving trooper and sends him off course.
The creature throws a boulder and knocks the trooper from his path.
The creature raises its cup toward the group and walks into the high country.
Indy returns photographs of the Tibetan men to Tsering.
Indy burns Kessler’s research folder to keep the mountain a rumor.
At dawn, bruised Pemba returns; enormous tracks cross the snowfield.
An empty tin cup lies in the tracks, marked with one new stroke.
Voss returns with his surviving men and demands the documents.
Stoll refuses to raise his rifle as the ridge falls silent.
At dawn, Tsering keeps Norbu’s photograph and confession close beneath the open pass.
On the flight out, Indy watches the peaks vanish into cloud beside Jo.

projets.pitch:
# The Roar of Two Kingdoms
*An original Lion Guard story — audiobook pitch (private, personal use)*

**Logline:** Years after the Tree of Life, King Kion must answer to two kingdoms at once. A pride born of drought is uniting the Outlands, and the only way to save both homes is the power he swore never to misuse: the Roar of the Elders.

**Hook:** Kion has a crown, his queen Rani, and a scar that still burns when he's angry. Kiara rules the Pride Lands with Kovu. When the rains fail in both realms, a new lioness, Zuri-Ama, gives starving Outsiders a home in the old volcano. War looms with Kion's own family on opposite sides, and the original Guard reunites for one last patrol.

## Why fans will love it
- The original Guard reunites.
- Kion and Kiara rule side by side.
- Ono's eyesight gets a heroic payoff.
- It answers whether the scar's venom is really gone, and bridges to the Lion King II timeline.
- Rani, Makini, Janja and Fuli all get real arcs.

## Cast
Kion, Rani, Kiara, Kovu, Bunga, Fuli, Beshte, Ono, Makini, Janja, Rafiki and Mufasa's spirit.
New: **Zuri-Ama**, an antagonist you end up feeling for, and **Tamu**, Rani's young cousin.

## Tone
A warm adventure for ages 8 and up, with grown-up themes of duty, grief and forgiveness.

## 14 chapters
1. Dry Season
2. Message from Pride Rock
3. The Volcano Pride
4. Old Friends
5. Janja's Warning
6. Split Council
7. Riverbed Ambush
8. Through Ono's Eyes
9. The Scar Wakes
10. Mufasa in the Clouds
11. Two Kingdoms March
12. Zuri-Ama's Truth
13. The Gentle Roar — Kion calls the storm instead of the army.
14. Rain on Both Kingdoms — Tamu joins the next Guard.

## Length
About 2 h 30, around 23,000 words (10–11 minutes per chapter).

## Narration
One warm Arena voice with light character voices: Bunga talks fast, Fuli is clipped, Beshte is slow, Zuri-Ama is low and kind. Savanna ambience between chapters; drums only for the Roar scenes. No Disney songs.
